messages.subject: user-defined functions for (a)(d)cast in reshape2
parts:
Users:

I'd like to call a user-defined function on my melt-ed data and I'm struggling to find a parallel example. Briefly I have melt-ed a
data frame and am trying to acast (or dcast) it with my own aggregating function that accepts a numerical vector (the value column) and a
logical vector in another column. The 'values' are selected by Type and Location (both factors) and I want to aggregate the corresponding
values according to the TRUE/FALSE in a column called 'Cens'

head(a.tmp)
             Type Location variable   value  Cens
1 Post-30 s flush      001   COPPER 0.08800 FALSE
2 Post-30 s flush      001     LEAD 0.00078 FALSE
3      First draw      001   COPPER 0.13000 FALSE
4      First draw      001     LEAD 0.00210 FALSE
5 Post-30 s flush      002   COPPER 0.02900 FALSE
6 Post-30 s flush      002     LEAD 0.00050  TRUE  #(note: at times, there is > 1 value for a Type/Location combination, hence the aggregation)
...

acast(a.tmp, Location ~ variable ~ Type, fun.aggregate=cmean, .(x=value, cens=Cens))

and cmean is a user defined function that accepts x and cens as parameters. Obviously this example is wrong and
  I'm hoping someone can point me to the right way. Here's cmean

cmean <- function(x,cens) {
  require(NADA)  # R library
  x.mle <- cenmle(x,cens)   # from NADA
  x.mean <- mean(x.mle)
  return(x.mean)
}

Thanks all.

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: user-defined functions for (a)(d)cast in reshape2
parts:
Could you supply a large enough sample of your a.tmp dataframe to do
something with?

I'm thinking you could do this differently with dplyr, but I'm not
sure if it really does what you want.

Something like:
library(NADA)
library(dplyr)

a.tmp %>%
group_by(Location, variable, Type) %>%
summarise(x.mle = cenmle(value, cens), x.mean = mean(x.mle))

Not completely sure though without data.

B

The idea was that, in the case where replicates were present with censoring, I'd use the cenmle or cenros procedure to get summary statistics that account for censoring. That's what prompted the query. So, it's a question of selecting the data like acast does, sending the selections to cmean, figuring out what to do, and then returning the summary statistics to put in the table that acast creates. There may be (usually is) a better way to do all this but I've used acast a bit with R/stats and other procedures with success, so I was starting there.
So, once I get acast (or whatever) to successfully call my procedure, I can move forward from there.

OK, I think maybe... maybe I've got it, but I need you to check it over. Previously, my map_dbl was incorrect. Not everthing is NA as I stated before.

I'll explain each line as I go:

#start with dataset
df1 %>%
# grouping variables
group_by(Location, variable, Type) %>%

# create a nested datatable per group
nest() %>%
# magic here. Map the output of cenmle to a data column
# second mutate takes this and extracts the mean of the result
# if you want SE or CIs you need to extract mean(x)[[2]], mean(x)[[3]], mean(x)[[4]]

mutate(
x.mle = map(data, function(x) {
with(x, cenmle(value, Cens))
}),

x.mean = map_dbl(x.mle, function(x) {
mean(x)[[1]] #first element is the mean
})
) %>%
#remove the x.mle column
select(-x.mle) %>%
# expand the data back out
unnest() %>%
# regroup the variables
group_by(Location, variable, Type) %>%

#take only first row, (removes duplicate rows with grouping combination)
slice(1) %>%
# replace value with x.mean when x.mean is not NaN
mutate(value = if_else(is.nan(x.mean), value, x.mean)) %>%
#clean up and get rid of x.mean column
select(-x.mean)


This should leave you with a dataframe/tibble that looks like the original one without the duplications and the mean values output from cenmle when appropriate. 

There may be a better/shorter way of doing this, but this seems to work. Please check the values and that it makes sense to you. 

HTH, 
B
